policy_name: ISO/IEC 23894:2023 Information technology — Artificial intelligence — Guidance on risk management
issuing_authority: ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42 (International Organization for Standardization and International Electrotechnical Commission)
regulatory_regime: Voluntary international guidance standard (not certifiable); AI-specific application of ISO 31000:2018
covered_entities: organizations that develop, produce, deploy or use products, systems and services that utilize AI
covered_systems: AI systems and AI-enabled products and services
covered_activities: integrating risk management into AI-related activities
risk identification, analysis, evaluation and treatment
conditions: Guidance only ('should' statements); intended to be tailored to the organization and its context
objective: Provide guidance on how organizations can manage risks specifically related to AI and integrate risk management into AI-related activities and functions, by adapting the principles, framework and process of ISO 31000:2018 to AI.
conflict_rule: Guidance standard; does not override legal requirements. Should be read with ISO 31000:2018, whose structure it follows.

sources_consulted: https://www.iso.org/standard/77304.html (catalogue page, via search results only)
record_provenance.notes: Paywalled standard: official text not accessed; all clauses are paraphrases (text_is_verbatim=false). Structure (Clause 4 Principles, Clause 5 Framework, Clause 6 Risk management process; Annex B risk sources; Annex C risk management and AI system life cycle) corroborated by the ANSI preview and OECD.AI summaries per search results. Annex A topic (AI-related objectives) reported inconsistently by secondary sources. Exact publication day not verified (only YYYY-MM given). Secondary sources (2026) report no amendment or revision in progress; a CEN adoption as EN ISO/IEC 23894 was mentioned by one source but could not be verified. Principles list mirrors ISO 31000:2018 principles, which 23894 adopts with AI-specific commentary. Official languages: only English edition confirmed.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] Top management should demonstrate leadership and commitment by integrating AI risk management into all organizational activities, issuing a statement or policy establishing an AI risk management approach, allocating resources, and assigning authority, responsibility and accountability for managing AI risks at appropriate levels.
clauses.action: demonstrate leadership, allocate resources, assign accountability
clauses.requirement: integrate AI risk management with clear accountability and resources
clauses.purpose: embed AI risk management in governance
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase following ISO 31000 clause 5.2 with AI-specific additions; subclause heading believed correct but not verified against the official text.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization should define the scope of its AI risk management activities, understand the external and internal context (including applicable legal requirements, stakeholder expectations and the AI system's intended purpose and use), and define risk criteria, including the amount and type of risk it may or may not take, taking into account impacts on individuals, groups and society.
clauses.action: define scope, context and risk criteria
clauses.requirement: set scope, context and risk criteria before assessing AI risk
clauses.purpose: tailor risk management to AI context
clauses.affected_asset: individuals, groups, society and the organization

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization should identify AI-related risks by considering assets and their value, risk sources (e.g. complexity of the environment, lack of transparency and explainability, level of automation, machine learning-specific issues, system hardware, lifecycle issues and technology readiness), potential events and outcomes, controls in place, and consequences for the organization, individuals and society.
clauses.object: AI risk sources, events, outcomes and consequences
clauses.requirement: systematically identify AI risks using AI-specific risk sources
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; the listed risk sources correspond to Annex B as summarized in secondary sources and should be verified.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization should select and implement options for treating AI risks (e.g. avoiding the risk, removing the risk source, changing likelihood or consequences, sharing the risk, or retaining it by informed decision), prepare risk treatment plans, and assess whether residual risk is acceptable, taking into account AI-specific considerations.
clauses.requirement: treat AI risks and evaluate residual risk
clauses.purpose: reduce AI risks to acceptable levels

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization should monitor and review the AI risk management process and its outcomes on an ongoing and periodic basis throughout the AI system life cycle, recognizing that AI systems and their context can change over time (e.g. through continuous learning or data drift).
clauses.object: AI risk management process and outcomes
clauses.requirement: continuously and periodically monitor AI risks across the lifecycle
clauses.purpose: keep risk management effective as AI systems evolve
clauses.affected_asset: AI system reliability and affected stakeholders
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; Annex C maps risk management activities to AI lifecycle stages.
